ratings_why.fun: Short clocks feeding Dripstone and the long Deep Vigils is a clear, satisfying puzzle, and the Eldest and Mother Ribica turns are big moments worth waiting for.
ratings_why.distinct: Countdowns and a game-long counter are familiar shapes (Dormant, spells-cast counts); the fresh parts are Deep Vigils fed by endings and the Robber-Knight paying for silence.

verdict_why: Three cards (Seven-Year Sitter, Brother Netopir, Comes-and-Goes Olm) can't be read as written; the core needs no change.

points.text: The Seven-Year Sitter's "numbers are doubled" can't be read: say on the card which numbers, for example "stat and gold gains in their Vigil effects are doubled".

Brother Netopir's "the last Vigil effect this turn" is hard to track in a cascade. Tie it to something on the board, for example "repeat the effect of the last unit whose Vigil ended this turn", and mark that unit on screen.
The Comes-and-Goes Olm doesn't say whether "the lake" is one per board or one per Olm, which matters with two copies. Make it one board-wide lake shown on the board.
The seed's "kept and left alone" shows only on the Robber-Knight. A Vigil that restarts when its unit is moved would make stillness a choice on every olm.
The Courier Bat is a generic buffer. As a messenger it could pass the word, for example: when a Vigil next to it ends, another unit next to it counts down by 1.

standouts.why: Gold for a silent turn: the flavour is the mechanic, and it reads in one line.
The Eldest's rare, huge answer is the seed's fantasy, in plain words.
A bite that grows with the age of the rumour: simple, funny and readable.

weakest.why: Generic "after X, buff a neighbour" with little bat or messenger in it.
Plain stat engine; the pilgrimage flavour doesn't show in what it does.
"+1/+1 for every 3 Dripstone" is more counter math, and overlaps "Baby Dragon".

flags.note: Which numbers double is not defined (the design's own risks say so).
Which effect is "last" in a chain of endings is hard to see.
One lake per board or one per Olm is not stated.
Repeating Mother Ribica or the Eldest doubles a capstone each time.
"Counts as every tribe" touches every other tribe's rules; a heavy read on edge cases.
